title: Register a Source Document by file upload
user_visible_behavior: An Operator attaches a PDF to a Party; its text is extracted with page mapping and the document reaches the `parsed` state.
verification: pytest with a fixture PDF: extracted text plus page numbers are stored and the state is `parsed`
A PDF with no text layer ends in the `failed` state with a reason
notes: No OCR in the MVP. Store a content hash.

title: Register a Source Document by URL
user_visible_behavior: An Operator registers a manifesto URL; it is fetched, parsed and stored with a content hash.
verification: pytest with a mocked HTTP response: the document reaches `parsed` with its hash
An HTTP error ends in `failed`
notes: Ingestion origin is configurable per document (upload | url).

title: Configurable LLM provider with a fake for tests
user_visible_behavior: The LLM provider and model are chosen by configuration; a deterministic fake provider is used in tests.
verification: pytest: the provider is resolved from config; the fake returns structured output
No test makes network calls to an LLM
notes: Implement at least one real provider adapter (e.g. Anthropic) behind the interface, with structured output.

title: Pipeline Run generates candidate Statements
user_visible_behavior: Running the pipeline for an Election produces a candidate Dataset Version containing topic-tagged Statements derived from the Source Documents.
verification: pytest with the fake provider: the run creates a Dataset Version in `candidate` with N Statements
The Pipeline Run moves through queued → running → validating
notes: Prompt rules: neutral wording, a single proposition per Statement. Version the prompts.

title: Pipeline Run extracts Party Positions with Evidence
user_visible_behavior: For every Statement and Party, the run stores a position (−2..+2 or no stance) with a verbatim quote and a page or URL locator.
verification: pytest with the fake provider: every Statement × Party pair has a position, and non-`no stance` positions have Evidence
notes: For coalitions, the joint manifesto takes precedence over member manifestos. Chunk long manifestos.

title: Validation verifies Evidence quotes exist in the source
user_visible_behavior: A run fails Validation when any Evidence quote isn't found in its Source Document text (normalized match), and the report names the offending positions.
verification: pytest: an invented quote → failed with a report entry; real quotes with whitespace or accent differences → pass
notes: Check 2 in docs/domain-model.md. The match tolerance is an implementation-time decision.

title: Validation enforces minimum Party coverage
user_visible_behavior: A run fails if any Party has positions on less than the configured share (default 70%) of Statements.
verification: pytest: a party with 60% coverage → failed; 70% → pass; the threshold can be configured
notes: Check 3. Initial position: fail the whole run.

title: Validation rejects Statements that don't separate parties
user_visible_behavior: A run fails if any Statement has the same position for every Party.
verification: pytest: one Statement with every position equal → failed with that Statement named
notes: Check 4. Positions of `no stance` are ignored for this check.

title: Validation checks Statement count, uniqueness and topic spread
user_visible_behavior: A run fails if the Statement count is out of range, Statements are duplicated, or one topic exceeds the configured share.
verification: pytest: 20 Statements → failed; duplicates → failed; 50% of Statements on one topic → failed; a valid set → pass
notes: Checks 1, 5 and 6. Detecting compound propositions can be heuristic.

title: Passing runs auto-publish; failing runs keep the previous version
user_visible_behavior: When every Validation check passes, the Dataset Version becomes Published and the previous one is superseded; when one fails, the previous Published version stays live.
verification: pytest: pass → published with exactly one Published version per Election; fail → previous version unchanged
notes: Superseded versions stay readable for old Share Links.

title: Operator can inspect a Pipeline Run report
user_visible_behavior: A CLI command shows a run's status, provider, model, prompt version, duration, token or cost estimate, and the Validation report.
verification: pytest: the report command prints the stored fields for a passed run and a failed run
notes: Observability per docs/technical-discovery.md. Read-only: AI output cannot be edited.

title: Live mode starts a run when a Source Document changes
user_visible_behavior: With GENERATION_MODE=live, adding a Source Document or changing its hash queues a Pipeline Run; with precomputed, it doesn't.
verification: pytest: live + new document → run queued; live + same hash → no run; precomputed → no run
notes: Never generates per user.

title: Live mode periodically re-fetches URL sources
user_visible_behavior: URL Source Documents are re-fetched at a configured interval; a changed hash updates the document and triggers regeneration.
verification: pytest with a mocked HTTP response and a controlled clock: changed content → new hash + run queued; same content → nothing
notes: The interval is configurable (e.g. 6h).

title: Public API serves a Dataset Version
user_visible_behavior: GET endpoints return active Elections, and the Questionnaire plus Party Positions with Evidence for the Published version or a specific version id.
verification: pytest: the published version is returned; a superseded version is still returned by id; an unknown id → 404
notes: Read-only and cacheable. No voter data in requests.

title: Landing page lets a Voter choose an Election

verification: pytest: the page renders the published Election and the disclosure
Manual check at 375px and desktop widths following DESIGN.md
notes: Follow DESIGN.md: neutral palette, no party colours.

title: Voter answers Statements on the 5-point scale

Network check: no request carries the answers
notes: The scale is an accessible radio group; no red/green.

title: Voter marks a Statement as Important

verification: Browser test: toggle the star, navigate, and the state is kept
notes: Amber accent is reserved for this (DESIGN.md).

title: Client-side Match Score calculation
user_visible_behavior: Given answers and positions, each Party gets a Match Score following the rule in docs/build-brief.md, with skip and no stance excluded, Important weighted ×2, and low coverage flagged.
verification: Unit tests for exact scores: identical answers → 100%, opposite → 0%, weighting, exclusions, and the low-coverage threshold
notes: Runs in the browser; it needs a JS unit-test runner wired into init.sh.

title: Results page shows the party ranking
user_visible_behavior: After the last Statement, the Voter sees Parties ordered by Match Score with percentage bars and a low-coverage badge; ties are alphabetical.
verification: Browser test with fixture data: the order and percentages match the engine's output
Skipping every Statement shows a prompt instead of a ranking
notes: No party colours on the bars.

title: Results breakdown shows each Party's Evidence
user_visible_behavior: For each Statement, the Voter sees their answer and each Party's position; expanding a position reveals the quote and a source link, or 'no stance in the manifesto'.
verification: Browser test: expanding a position shows the quote and a working locator; no stance is labelled
notes: Quotes use a serif font (DESIGN.md).

title: Voter copies a Share Link of their result
user_visible_behavior: A share button copies a URL that encodes the Dataset Version id and the answers in the fragment, with a note that nothing is stored.
verification: Unit test: the encode/decode round-trip is lossless, including skip and Important
The answers appear only after `#`
notes: Version the encoding format.

title: Opening a Share Link reproduces the result
user_visible_behavior: Opening a Share Link shows the same ranking and breakdown for that Dataset Version; if it has been superseded, a notice offers the current questionnaire.
verification: Browser test: the shared URL renders identical scores
A superseded version shows the notice; a malformed link shows a friendly error
